decks.label: Sillabe → parole · ca me lu so
decks.comboAudit: All 64 combinations enumerated and screened for vulgar/slur/anatomy surfaces — none composable: no ce/ci/ge/gi (soft c/g held back for a later deck), no cu, and the two syllable sets never repeat a column-1 syllable in column 2 in a way that lets cacca/pipì-class words form. Rare-but-attested forms kept real so no dictionary word is ever labelled a robot word: mena (menare), mene and mane (letterari, Treccani), maso (regionale, Treccani), rasa, raso, rata, meta. nana/nano/nane kept plain real — standard K-1 fairy-tale register (i sette nani).
decks.notes: Starter deck of the metodo fono-sillabico: sillabe piane a+o dominant, all consonants continuous-or-familiar (c only before a/o = hard /k/). 33/64 real — the densest CVCV space we could close vulgarity-free.

decks.label: Sillabe con i · e — pino, vela, nido
decks.comboAudit: All 56 combinations enumerated and screened. Flagged sensitive (real words, kept out of chains): peto (dictionary word, scatological), seno (anatomy, also the math term). Robot combos screened and judged inert in Italian: pedo (prefix only, no standalone slang currency in Italian), seso (distinct from sesso — single s, different syllable weight), dira (dirà needs the accent). pipì is structurally impossible (no pi in column 2). dino kept robot (informal truncation, not a lemma). Rare-but-attested kept real: pilo and pira (Treccani), verb forms vedo, rido, sedo, peno, pela, dite.
decks.notes: Extends the vowel space to i/e with the new continuous consonants v, d, r in onset. 25/56 real; four picture badges (dito, nido, pera, riso).

decks.label: Trisillabe · ba-na-na, ma-ti-ta
decks.comboAudit: All 18 combinations enumerated and screened — no vulgar/slur/anatomy surface in the space. batata (patata dolce, Treccani) and panata (minestra di pane, Treccani) kept real so they are never labelled robot words; patina, patita, manata real. matina kept robot on purpose: it is the classic single-t misspelling of mattina and makes a useful doppie teaching moment.
decks.notes: Tight 3×3×2 trisyllable space over the three classroom words banana, patata, matita — the classic parole piane trisillabe of classe prima primers. Column 3 role syl3 has no colSyl3 UI string yet (falls back to the onset label); flagged upstream.

decks.label: Le doppie · gat-to, pal-la, pen-na
decks.comboAudit: All 64 combinations enumerated and screened. Flagged sensitive: palle (the normal plural of palla, but a common vulgar surface — kept real, kept out of chains). The tet- onset was rejected at design time because tetta would be composable. Robot combos screened and judged inert: palto/palta (paltò needs the accent), galto/gonso-class strings. pento (mi pento), polla/polle (vena d'acqua sorgiva, Treccani) kept real. Every geminate word splits the doppia across the card seam exactly as Italian syllabification prescribes: gat-to, gat-ta, pal-la, gal-la/gal-lo, pen-na/pen-ne, sas-so, pol-lo, col-la/col-le/col-lo, gon-na/gon-ne; the closed-syllable combos without geminate (pen-so, col-to, col-ta, pol-so) are also true syllable splits.
decks.notes: The moat deck: the doppia lives on the seam between the two cards, so sweeping across it makes the long consonant audible (gat…to). 23/64 real, six picture badges.
